q1.answer: No. ADR013 (node-fetch) is marked superseded in its own text by ADR014. ADR014 says frontend plugins and packages should prefer the fetchApiRef (which NotificationsClient's injected fetchApi matches), while Node.js backend/CLI code should use native fetch instead of third-party libraries like node-fetch.

q2.answer: ADR007 requires all fetch/XMLHttpRequest calls in tests to be mocked using msw. Per its Context, this avoids the 'total pain' of every type of test (unit through e2e) having its own, inconsistent implementation of request mocking, replacing that mix of ad hoc approaches with one consistent express-style route-declaration pattern.

q3.answer: ADR006 cites that React.FC implicitly added children props to the component's prop types, and that it did not support a generic type on children. The concrete upstream fact given is that Facebook/Create React App removed React.FC from its base TypeScript template because it was found to have next to no benefit with these downsides.

q4.answer: The library being replaced is Moment.js. ADR010 gives two reasons it's being retired: it's affected by large bundle sizes, and it has mutable-state issues; separately, the Moment.js project itself is being sunset and recommends switching to a modern alternative.

q5.answer: ADR004 (Module Export Structure) requires every exported symbol to be traceable through index files all the way to the package root src/index.ts, with each index file re-exporting only from its immediate directory children. It was meant to make it easy to answer the question 'Is the export in this module also exported by the package?' (equivalently, what is exported from this directory).

q6.answer: No -- under ADR004's rule, if any index file in the chain toward the root doesn't re-export a symbol (or the index file doesn't exist at all, as with a missing src/utils/index.ts), that symbol is not publicly exported, regardless of whether it was explicitly marked private. Since src/utils/index.ts doesn't exist and src/index.ts never mentions these files, notificationLinks.ts and plainText.ts are internal implementation details, not part of the public API.

q7.answer: ADR011 says an x-react package is for shared widgets, hooks, and similar code that both the plugin itself (x) and third-party frontend plugins can depend on. For notifications to need a notifications-react package, some of its components/hooks would have to be needed by other, third-party frontend plugins outside the notifications plugin itself.

q8.answer: ADR003 allows default exports only when 'absolutely necessary', citing React.lazy modules as the example. For teams wanting to avoid even that, it gives a workaround: wrap the dynamic import in a .then() that maps the named export to a synthetic { default: m.Component } object before passing it to React.lazy.

q9.answer: ADR015. Its Consequences section says the new loader/component option pattern will only be applied to APIs in the new frontend system (@backstage/frontend-* packages) and explicitly states existing APIs in the old frontend system (@backstage/core-* packages, which is the style the dev app uses) will not be updated/retrofitted.
